first-run.title: First run and the sample company
captions: The Workspace page is where questionnaires start. The menu on the left lists every task, grouped by area.
Start with the sample company runs a complete example on a fictional company, with nothing to set up.
When the run finishes, the summary shows how many questions have a proposed answer and what needs a person.

appearance-and-shortcuts.title: Appearance and quick actions
captions: The Dark mode switch at the bottom of the menu changes the appearance. The choice is remembered.
Press Ctrl and K (Command and K on a Mac), or click the search box at the top, to open the quick action list.
Type part of a task name and press Enter to go straight to it.

create-library.title: Create your answer library
captions: Your approved answers live in one spreadsheet. On the Workspace page, Create a new one makes it from a template.
The file my_approved_answers.csv is created in your results folder, and that folder opens so you can fill it in.
The card now shows the new library. Fill in one row per approved answer. Change lets you choose another file later.

build-library.title: Build your library from past questionnaires
captions: Build your library recovers the answers from questionnaires your team completed before.
Click the card and choose a completed questionnaire in Excel format.
Click Recover answers. The answers are saved to approval_candidates.csv for your team to approve.

library-health.title: Check library health
captions: Library health checks the approved answers themselves. Choose your library, then click Check library.
The tiles count active, shareable, expiring and expired approvals, and rows set aside for safety.
Each note below names the row and what to do about it, for example an approval that has expired.

guard-terms.title: Guard terms
captions: Guard terms are words your team treats like certifications. Put them in guard_terms.txt next to your library.
Library health lists the guard terms it found, here HIPAA and 24/7.
An answer that uses a guard term your approved answers do not support is marked At risk.

answer-questionnaire.title: Answer a questionnaire
captions: Click the first card and choose the buyer's questionnaire, in Excel or CSV format, exactly as they sent it.
Click the second card and choose your approved answers.
Save results in shows where the finished files go. Click Change to pick another folder.
Click Answer questionnaire. Each question is checked against your library as the run progresses.
The summary counts each status. Open report shows every question with its status and evidence.

review-and-edit.title: Review and edit answers
captions: Review and edit lists every question. The filters narrow the list, for example to questions that need a person.
Type in the search box to find a question or answer by any word.
Select a question to see its answer beside the approved evidence. Edit the text and it is checked as you type.
Use approved wording puts back the approved text. Clear empties the answer, and Revert to original undoes your edits.

export-final.title: Export the final file
captions: When the review is done, click Export final file.
A copy of the buyer's file is written with your final answers, and every answer is checked once more.
The result says whether the file is ready to send and lists anything that still needs attention.

check-before-sending.title: Check before sending
captions: Check before sending takes the final file you are about to send, including edits made outside the app.
Choose the final file and your approved answers, then click Run the check.
Each finding names the question and the claim your approved answers do not support.
Open pre-send report shows the full check, ready to keep with the questionnaire.

trust-pack.title: Customer trust pack
captions: Mark customer safe rows shareable=yes in your library. Then choose the library and enter your company name.
Click Build trust pack. Private and expired answers are left out automatically.
Open trust pack shows the page to review and then send to your customer yourself.

ai-cloud.title: AI with a cloud service
captions: AI drafting is optional. To use a cloud service, open AI drafting and choose the service, for example Anthropic.
Paste your API key and click Save key. The key is stored on this computer only. No key is entered in this guide.
Enter the model name or click Load list. Then tick the box that allows sending questions to that service.
Test connection sends one test question. Use this model turns drafting on for every questionnaire.

ai-local.title: AI on your computer
captions: To keep everything on your computer, run a model with llama.cpp, Ollama or LM Studio and choose it here.
Enter the address of the model server and the model name, then click Test connection.
Click Use this model. From now on, questions that only partly match your library get a drafted answer.
Every draft is checked against the approved answer it cites before you see it. Drafted answers are marked Drafted.

ai-off.title: Turn AI drafting off
captions: In use now shows the model that drafts answers. Turn off AI stops drafting at any time.
With AI turned off, answers come only from your approved library, word for word.

command-line.title: Command line
captions: Every task is also available from the command line, for scripts and scheduled jobs.

troubleshooting.title: Troubleshooting
captions: If an ad blocker or web filter blocks part of the app, the app reloads itself up to two times.
If it is still blocked, this message explains which setting to change in the ad blocker.

install.title: Install and uninstall on Windows
captions: Open the installer. Keep the suggested folder, which installs the app for your user account only, and click Next.
Tick Create a desktop shortcut if you want one, then click Next.
Check the summary and click Install.
Leave Open Questionnaire Autopilot now ticked and click Finish.
The app opens on the Overview page. Later, open it from the Start menu or the desktop shortcut.
To uninstall, choose Uninstall in Settings, then Apps. Windows asks you to confirm.
The app is removed. Your settings stay until you delete their folder.
install.note: Installer screens. The install folder path is pixelated because it contains the Windows user name.

intellinaire-chat.title: Intellinaire, the assistant
captions: Intellinaire is the assistant under Intellinaire in the menu. It uses the model set up on the AI drafting page.
Ask a question about your work. It reads the last run, your review and your library to answer.
Each step it takes is listed as it happens. The reply is written as it streams in.
To change something, ask for it. Intellinaire prepares the change and checks it with the claim guard.
The proposal shows the new wording, marked against the current answer, with the claim guard's verdict. Nothing has changed yet.
Approve applies the change. Reject leaves everything as it was.
Attach files or images with these buttons, by dragging them onto the chat, or by pasting.
Search the web lets it look online for this message only. Turn it on before you send.
Every conversation is kept on this computer. The menu beside it renames, pins, copies or deletes it.

library-atlas.title: The library atlas
captions: The Workspace page shows your approved answers as an atlas. Each point is one answer, grouped by topic.
Point at an answer to see its question. Click it to read the answer, its evidence, approver and expiry.
Ask Intellinaire opens the chat with a question about that answer.
Click a topic to show only its answers. Click it again to show all.
Find an answer searches every question and answer. Hold Ctrl and scroll, or use the buttons, to zoom.
During a run, each question travels to the answers it used, in the colour of its result.

overview.title: The security program overview
captions: The Overview page is the start of your security program. Until you set it up, it offers the sample company.
Explore the sample company loads a complete program for Examplify Inc., a fictional company.
The top row shows the posture score, open risks, vendors due for review, open incidents and what is due in 30 days.
Readiness lists every framework you track. Next deadlines lists incident notifications and recurring activities.
Below, the most valuable next steps and the risk heat map. Every item opens its own page.

company-profile.title: Company profile
captions: The company profile decides which frameworks, notification deadlines and policy wording apply.
Choose the data you hold, where you operate and the rules that apply to you. Each choice is saved at once.
Then choose the frameworks customers, regulators or insurers hold you to.

frameworks.title: Framework readiness
captions: Frameworks shows readiness requirement by requirement. Each tab is one framework you track.
Gaps lists the requirements no safeguard covers yet. Each safeguard name opens it on the Safeguards page.
ISO 27001 covers all 93 Annex A controls. Export readiness workbook saves every framework and the Statement of Applicability.

safeguards.title: Assess safeguards
captions: Safeguards lists 44 controls grouped by area. You assess each one once, and it counts toward every framework.
Select a safeguard to see what in place means, then set its status, owner and evidence.
The posture score and every framework's readiness update as you go. The page lists the frameworks it counts toward.

policies.title: Security policies
captions: Policies lists fifteen security policies written from your company profile and safeguards.
Select a policy to read it, with its owner, rules for each safeguard and framework references.
Approve it with the approver's name and version. Its yearly review then appears on the calendar.
Write all policies saves every policy as a Word document, HTML and Markdown in your results folder.

risks.title: Risk register
captions: The risk register lists each risk with its score, treatment, owner and due date. Overdue dates are marked.
Risks your safeguard gaps imply are suggested below. Add puts one in the register with its rating.
Edit the owner, due date and treatment, then Save. The heat map shows where the open risks sit.

vendors.title: Vendor risk
captions: Vendors lists each supplier with a tier set by the data it holds, its access, criticality and integration.
Northwind IT Services has administrator remote access, so it is Critical and has never been reviewed.
Create questionnaire saves an Excel questionnaire sized to the tier. Score their answers reads it back with red flags.
Reviewed today records the review; the next one appears on the calendar.

incidents.title: Incident response
captions: Incidents opens with the current incident: what happened, its severity, status and the data involved.
Notification deadlines count down for each party that may need to be told, from your profile and the incident.
Work through the playbook steps. Each one is ticked with its time and kept with the incident.
Record an incident starts a new one. Choose its kind, severity and when you became aware; the deadlines start then.

calendar-reports.title: Calendar and reports
captions: The calendar lists recurring activities, vendor reviews and policy reviews, overdue first.
Done records the date an activity was carried out, which sets its next due date.
Reports creates the security posture report for leadership and the readiness workbook for auditors.
